content.text: Can you try this with a policy that doesn't specify a subject?
I think there is a related bug that has to do with generating checksums, but I'd like to check in on the original problem description here first.

Thanks for helping me debug, Scott.  I'm attaching a patch that should address this problem (and another involving checksums on referenced file content).  I think it's ready to go, but it seems like a bad idea to commit to trunk at 4:30 on a Friday.  If you want to try this out, I'm all ears.

the diagnosis, for what it's worth: The original patch that allowed file uri's passed the dsLocation into the authorization module as a PID, which was a hack because I didn't want to add a new method to the Authorization interface.  Unfortunately, the assignment stayed there after the auth was done properly, doing nothing in 3.3, but suddenly causing problems in 3.4 with the object policies being fetched by Akubra.  I'll fill in more details on the Tuesday call next week.
I downloaded and installed the patch, then ran my tests again.  This time they succeeded:  I was able to create and view both managed and externally-managed datastreams with a file:// URL.

I then modified the test policy to specify a bogus allowed file path, and ran the tests again.  All of them failed, as expected, except for one:  I was able to create an externally-managed datastream with a file:// URL that did not match the allowed pattern in the policy (I was not able to subsequently view it, however).  So it appears the policy isn't getting applied when creating externally-managed datastreams?

External and redirected datastreams aren't checked against policies until they're accessed (either as a dissemination or to generate a checksum).  I'll look into how feasible it is to check them against the policies on creation instead.

When I compile the code with mvn clean install, I get the following compilation errors:
Am I missing something? I installed using the Fedora 3.4 source release.
Did you run "mvn clean install -P fedora-installer" from the top level of your fedora source directory (/home/lengelbrecht/Fedora3.4_src/fcrepo-src-3.4)?
Current status: We think this was fixed by FCREPO-822, would like to verify....so will add a test case for this.
Writing this test is tricky- the test needs a supporting XACML policy that refers to the canonical path of the test resource. The fix is in 3.5, but the test is in the 3.6 bucket.
This should be verifiable in the tests in TestExternalDatastreams now

When policy enforcement is turned on, and there is a policy in place to allow file uploads from specified paths, only an authenticated user is allowed to see the created externally-managed datastream.  Attached is a transcript of what takes place, but in summary, I'm allowed, as fedoraAdmin, to create objects with M and E datastreams whose content is uploaded via the file URI;  however, when I attempt to view the Externally Managed datastreams (E) as an unauthenticated anonymous user, I get a "Policy blocked datastream resolution" exception in the logs, caused by a "AuthzDeniedException":
If I retrieve the E datastream authenticated as the fedoraAdmin, then I can see it.  Datastreams of other types within the same object are visible to the world, as expected.

Creation of externally-managed datatstreams that use a file URI should be controlled by the file-resolution policies, but once the datastreams are created, they should be visible to the world according to the same rules that apply to M, R, and X datastreams in an object.
See attachments for a transcript of a test showing this behavior, and a sample policy file that replaces deny-unallowed-file-resolution.xml.
